text:
mike: Heads-up — ran into a sneaky goroutine leak in the Go generator streaming sample app when auth refresh happens mid-stream. repro steps below.

mike: Repro: run the example with short token TTL so refresh triggers during a long generation
`go run ./examples/gen-stream-auth-refresh --ttl 5s --prompt 'long story'`

mike: Logs show repeated goroutine stacks growing after each refresh:
```
leak: goroutine 54 [chan receive]:
  main.(*streamWorker).run(0xc0001...)
  runtime.goexit
created by main.startWorker
  main.startWorker(0xc000...)
```

tess: thanks — can you paste the minimal snippet you're using to consume the generator stream?

mike: sure — simplified: 
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
for chunk := range stream.Chunks() {
  fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}
// we never see a final error if auth refresh failed mid-stream
```

sanjay: hmm. I think the issue is that our internal auth refresher replaces an internal transport ctx but doesn't close the upstream chunk channel when a mid-request refresh triggers a retry. So consumer goroutines can get stuck waiting on `stream.Chunks()` while the background worker is blocked.

lin: this sounds like a classic ownership/close contract mismatch. Right now Generator.Stream returns a channel-based iterator and relies on caller cancel to tear things down. But when the SDK initiates a transparent retry/refresh, it doesn't propagate an explicit terminal error to the iterator.

tess: user impact: onboarding friction — sample app never finishes and newbies think SDK is broken. We should do one of: (a) document the current behavior clearly, (b) change API to make lifecycle explicit, or (c) ensure internal refresh never leaves stream in limbo. Preference: (b) + (c).

mike: proposal: change Stream API to return a typed handle with Close() and Err() methods, e.g.:
```
type GenStream interface {
  Chunks() <-chan Chunk
  Close() error // stops internal goroutines and waits for shutdown
  Err() error   // final error after Close/drain
}
```
This makes cancellation explicit and lets us surface auth/retry errors.

lin: +1. Also we should document pattern: use context for request lifetime and call Close in a defer so both local cancel and SDK-initiated retries are handled. Example:
```
stream, _ := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
defer stream.Close()
for c := range stream.Chunks() { ... }
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil { return err }
```

sanjay: implementation note: easiest fix short-term is to ensure internal auth refresh returns a terminal error on streams that are mid-request and cannot be transparently retried. Longer-term: implement handle with explicit Close semantics.

mike: agree. Also add a small sample app `examples/gen-stream-auth-refresh` to the repo that demonstrates proper pattern (defer Close, check Err) so onboarding isn't blocked. New quickstart should highlight token TTL and how to set `REDWOOD_TOKEN_REFRESH_THRESHOLD`.

tess: action items:
- sanjay: open GH issue with repro, logs, and suggested API change (assign to eng-runtime).
- lin: draft sample app and quickstart snippet.
- mike: add failing test in the sample-app CI so we don't regress.
- @ci-bot: please run `examples/gen-stream-auth-refresh` on the small instance when PR lands.

ci-bot: CI job queued: examples/gen-stream-auth-refresh — will post results when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

lin: btw, small UX nit — our Go docs currently only show `Stream(ctx)` usage without Close. I'll patch docs to the explicit handle example.

mike: thanks all. If someone wants to pair on the short-term fix later today ping me. :thumbsup:
